1 1.

This is a reference petition u/s 18 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter referred to as "the Act"), filed by the petitioners mentioned aforesaid for enhancement of compensation awarded by the Land Acquisition Collector (NorthWest) (hereinafter called 'the LAC') for acquisition of their land for public purpose.
The petition was filed before the LAC and referred to by the Collector for determination of the court.

2. The brief factual matrix leading to the present petition is that the Government vide notification bearing No. F.11(19)/2001/L&B/LA/20112 dt. 21.03.2003 issued by the Lt. Governor of Delhi under Section 4 of the Act, Government intended to acquire about 2480 Bigha 01 Biswas of land LAC no.
321/ 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW))

Balwant Singh & Ors. Vs. Union of India Page no. 2 of 11 with its specification mentioned in the notification for public purpose namely 'Rohini Residential Scheme' under the "Planned Development of Delhi".

entities.text: Balwant Singh & Ors. Vs. Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 3. The Government vide consequent Declaration/notification No. F.11 (19)/2001/L&B/LA/28176 dated 19.03.2004 issued pursuant thereto under Section 6 of the Act, acquired 2480 Bigha 01 Biswas land (as detailed in the statement under Section 19 of the Act), situated in the revenue estate of village Mubarakpur Dabas, Delhi.

The LAC (N/W) after completing all the requisite formalities as provided under the Act, announced the Award bearing no. 16 of 200506 dated 14.09.2005 u/s 11 of the Act in respect of 2480 bighas 01 biswas out of the aforesaid said land and awarded a compensation at the uniform rate of Rs.15,70,000/ per acre (or Rs. 3,27,083.33/ per bigha) for the entire said land in addition to other statutory benefits and interests.

4. It is stated that the petitioners are the recorded owner/bhumidhar of the land comprised in Khasra no. 4//19 (416), 20/2 (112), 8//18 (416), 26//21/1 (28), 23//3 (21) i.e. total measuring 15 Bigha and 13 Biswas, having 1/3rd share each, situated in the revenue estate of Village Mubarakpur Dabas, Delhi (in short, the said land).
5.

It is stated that the Award passed by the ld. LAC is not acceptable to the petitioners and,
therefore, this reference has been filed with a view to LAC no. 321/ 2016 (Award No. 16/2005 06/DC(NW)) Balwant Singh & Ors. Vs.
Union of India
Page no. 3 of 11 reassess the market value of the land which has been wrongly assessed by the LAC.

6. Following are the grounds under which the reference petition has been filed :
i) The LAC has not adopted correct method of assessment of market value of the said land on imaginary basis and on the basis of a government police.
The market value of the acquired land is only to be assessed and determined strictly as provided by law U/s 23 and 24 of LA Act, 1894.
ii) The LAC has not considered the location, developments, existing utility and potentiality of the land.
The present physical and existing location, developments and the utility and potentiality of the land, in and around the land of the petitioners were not taken into account.
Balwant Singh Ors. (1605-06) vs Union Of India (Mubarakpur Dabas) on 7 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110644848/

entities.text: Balwant Singh Ors. (1605-06) vs Union Of India (Mubarakpur Dabas)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 2 iii) The LAC has erred in not taking into consideration the future potentiality and the utility of the acquired land of the petitioners.

The impugned award is arbitrary,
malafide and detrimental to the interest of the petitioners i.e. farmers.

The land of the petitioners has an increasing trend as regard to the market value after fixation of the rates of the agricultural land in Delhi and such rates have been increased by more than ten times.
The land of the petitioners have a very high value and is very fertile and leveled without any kind of depression or defect.
The said land be used for industrial or commercial or residential use with little efforts.
iv) The land of the petitioners is adjacent to welldeveloped areas, colonies and village Abadi and hence has a great market value.

The land LAC no. 321/ 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW))
Balwant Singh & Ors. Vs. Union of India Page no. 4 of 11 enjoys all type of facilities/ civic amenities like developed metalled roads, electricity, hospitals, government schools, public schools, computer institutes, full fledged post office, health gym, modern panchayat ghar, and most frequently served by DTC and various other private transporters as GT Road i.e. NH10, DelhiFirozpur Railway Line and main DelhiKanjhawala road passes by the side of village Mubarakpur Dabas.

entities.text: Balwant Singh & Ors. Vs. Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: There are nationalised bank operating with well established hospital and fully developed markets in village Mubarakpur Dabas.

Land is also surrounded by Ghevara Industrial Area, Savada Industrial Area,
Mundka Industrial Area with several godowns which are adjacent to the said village.

Government has provided all civic amenities like roads, transportation, electricity, water connections, schools,
hospitals, telecommunications, etc where the market value is more than Rs. 10,000/ per sq. yards.
Therefore, the price of the acquired land should have been assessed minimum @ Rs 10,000/ per sq. yards.
v) The LAC has not taken into consideration the relevant sale/purchase transactions of the land in village Mubarakpur Dabas and in the adjoining villages itself.

LAC has not announced any compensation for he standing crop of the petitioners and besides this, the petitioner were fully dependent upon their agricultural land which has been acquired and not the petitioners are left without any source of income.
Now, since they have to change their place of dwelling and setup a different business as well, the petitioners are entitled to a compensation of Rs. 1,00,000/.

Further,
an LAC no. 321/ 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Balwant Singh & Ors. Vs. Union of India Page no. 5 of 11 amount of Rs. 1,00,000/ should be granted to the petitioners for damages and substantial loss suffered as a result of severance of their leftover land.
vi) The LAC has not considered the increase of 15 % per annum in the value of the land between the date of notification and the date of announcement of the Award.

entities.text: Balwant Singh & Ors. Vs. Union of India

sentences.text: It is alleged that the LAC further has assessed the compensation merely on the basis of surmises and conjuctures and without looking into the actual market rate of land prevailing in the area.

7. It is stated that in view of these facts and circumstances and keeping in view the consideration of the petitioners, petitioners are claiming compensation for their acquired land at Rs. 10,000/ per sq. yards.

The petitioners also claim Rs. 10,000/ per Bigha for the loss of damage sustained by the Balwant Singh Ors. (1605-06) vs Union Of India (Mubarakpur Dabas) on 7 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110644848/
3 petitioners with regard to standing crops and vegetables.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioners also claim compensation of Rs. 10,00,000/ for standing trees, boundary and structure thereupon.
The petitioners further claim Rs. 10,00,000/ for tubewell/ well.
The respondents be directed to provide an alternative plot of reasonable size.
The petitioners have also claimed solatium @ 50% of the M. V. in addition to market value of land of petitioners alongwith statutory benefits as per law.

8. Opportunity to file Written statement on behalf of respondent no.1 i.e. Union of India was closed vide order dated 17.09.2014.
LAC no. 321/ 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Balwant Singh & Ors. Vs. Union of India Page no. 6 of 11 9.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Written statement has been filed on behalf of respondent no.2/DDA and, inter alia, it is submitted that the ld. LAC while passing the impugned Award in respect of village Mubarakpur Dabas had taken into consideration the market value of the land on the basis of the sale deeds of the adjoining lands of the area as well as the other documents which were made available to ld. LAC.
The area of the land and other amenities/facilities were also taken into consideration while assessing the compensation.

10. It is submitted that the compensation awarded by ld. LAC is adequate, sufficient just and legal and is based on cogent and reliable evidence, therefore, there is no scope for enhancement of the compensation amount.
The present reference petition is also barred by limitation.

The copy of the reference petition has not been forwarded to DDA, though the DDA is a beneficiary party, therefore,
DDA is not liable to pay any interest on the delayed period.

It is submitted that as per the directions of Land and Building Department, after announcement of the Award reference should be forwarded by LAC within 60 days from the date of filing of the reference.
The present petition has not been forwarded to the court within 60 days therefore, DDA/beneficiary of land is not liable to pay interest thereupon.
The petitioner is also not admitted to be the owner/Bhumidhar with respect to the said land and has no locus standi to file the present petition for enhancement of compensation.
LAC no. 321/ 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Balwant Singh & Ors. Vs. Union of India Page no. 7 of 11 11.

entities.text: Balwant Singh & Ors. Vs. Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is stated that the possession of the said land bearing Khasra No. 4/19 (416), 20/02 (112) has been taken over by the DDA on 04.04.2006 and after taking possession, the same was handed over to RPDVII.
The possession of Khasra No. 8/18 (416), 26/21/1 (208), 23/3 (21) could not be taken due to builtup.
As per the statement U/s 19 of LA Act, Khasra No. 23/3 measuring 2 Bigha and 1 Biswa is under the ownership of Gram Sabha.

All the other averments made by the petitioner in the reference petition were denied in toto and it is prayed that the prayer of the petitioner is false,
frivolous and vexatious and without any cause of action, therefore, the reference petition filed by the petitioner is level to be dismissed with cost.
12.
On the basis of pleadings of the parties and documents filed on record, the following issues were framed by the court on 17.09.2014:  ISSUES

13. Matter was listed for recording of petitioners evidence.

Ld. Counsel for the petitioner as well as Ld. Counsel for the respondents have submitted that they are relying upon the upon the evidence led by them in case bearing LAC no. 195 of 2016, Savitri Devi Vs. Union of India.

entities.text: Savitri Devi Vs. Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, no specific separate additional evidence for enhancement of compensation has been led.
LAC no. 321/ 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Balwant Singh & Ors. Vs. Union of India Page no. 8 of 11 14.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: I have heard the Ld. Counsels for the parties and have perused the entire record including the documents and the evidence led by the parties.
I have given a thoughtful consideration to the same.

My issue wise findings and determination are as under : 
1.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for enhancement in compensation, if yes, then to what extent?
OPP 15.
The onus of proving the aforesaid issue is on the petitioners.
16. To prove its case, the petitioner, through his counsel have adopted the evidence led in case Savitri Devi (supra).
During the course of arguments, he has relied upon the judgment passed in the aforementioned case on 05.09.2023 and Ld.
Counsel for the petitioner has argued that the petitioners may also be awarded compensation as awarded to the petitioners in the aforementioned case.
17. Even, the respondents have also relied upon the evidence led by the respondents in the aforementioned case and no separate evidence has been led by them in the present case.

18. Since the fair market value of the land situated in village Mubarakpur Dabas is covered by the award in question has already been LAC no. 321/ 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Balwant Singh & Ors. Vs. Union of India Page no. 9 of 11 determined by this court, this court has no reason or evidence to deviate therefrom.

entities.text: Balwant Singh & Ors. Vs. Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of the aforesaid discussion, this court also determines the same enhanced market value in the present case, in so far as the acquisition of the land of petitioners is concerned.

19. In the case of Savitri Devi (supra), this court had adjudicated the market value of land of village Mubarkpur Dabas acquired through Award No. 16 of 200506 dated 14.09.2005 as Rs. 19,45,800/
per acre i.e. an enhancement of Rs. 3,75,800/ per acre has been given.
There is no evidence on record to gather that the land of the petitioners herein was in any way inferior to the land involved in Savitri Devi (supra).
The petitioners are, accordingly entitled to the same compensation for their land as was awarded in Savitri Devi (supra).

This court adjudicate the market value of land of the Balwant Singh Ors. (1605-06) vs Union Of India (Mubarakpur Dabas) on 7 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110644848/
5 petitioners as Rs.19,45,800/ per acre thereby giving an enhancement of Rs.3,75,800/ per acre.
20.

entities.text: Balwant Singh Ors. (1605-06) vs Union Of India (Mubarakpur Dabas)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioners have not led any evidence with respect to alleged damages of the growing crops and structures or other claims.
Therefore, the petitioners shall not be entitled to any damages on the aforesaid counts.
This issue is decided accordingly in favour of the petitioners.
ISSUE NO. 2/ RELIEF 21.
As per the reference petition forwarded by LAC, the possession of land bearing Khasra No. 8/18 (416), 26/21/1 (208), 23/3 (21) has not LAC no. 321/ 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW))
Balwant Singh & Ors. Vs.
Union of India Page no. 10 of 11 been taken which has been admitted by the petitioner.
Further, as per the statement U/s 19 of LA Act, Khasra No. 23/3 measuring 2 Bigha and 1 Biswa is under the ownership of Gram Sabha.
Therefore, petitioner is not entitled for enhancement of compensation qua this land.

22. In view of the findings on Issue No.1, the petitioners are granted the following reliefs: (1) Fair Market value of land of petitioners as mentioned in the revised statement u/s 19 of the Act @
Rs.19,45,800/- per acre.
An enhancement of Rs.3,75,800/- per acre is accordingly accorded.
(2) Additional amount @ 12% ( in terms of Section 23 (1A) of the Act).

(3) Solatium @ 30% on the enhanced compensation (in terms of S.23 (2)
 of the Act).
(4) Interest @ 9% per annum for the first year and 15% per annum for the subsequent year till the payment of enhanced compensation by LAC is made (in terms of Section 28 of the Act).
23.
Reference petition is accordingly, answered with parties to bear their own respective costs.
Decree sheet be drawn accordingly.
File be consigned to record room after due compliance.

Rs.19,45,800/- per acre.
An enhancement of Rs.3,75,800/- per acre is accordingly accorded.
(2) Additional amount @ 12% ( in terms of Section 23 (1A) of the Act).

(3) Solatium @ 30% on the enhanced compensation (in terms of S.23 (2)
 of the Act).
(4) Interest @ 9% per annum for the first year and 15% per annum for the subsequent year till the payment of enhanced compensation by LAC is made (in terms of Section 28 of the Act).
23.
Reference petition is accordingly, answered with parties to bear their own respective costs.
